paragraphs.source_en: The most widely accepted theory is that pottery was invented for food processing, especially for cooking liquids, thus being a strong indicator of a change in food habits (Roset 1983; Hachid 1998; Aumassip 2006). This new technology enabled a range of new foods to be processed, which could not be done on direct fire or through stone boiling. The "culinary" origin of pottery containers is supported by the fact that it appeared at the same time as the grinding stones, probably used for crushing wild cereals. The changes in subsistence strategies caused the intensified use of wild grasses in the Epipalaeolithic and mainly in the Mesolithic period. The sustained boiling necessary for breaking down cereals into edible starch, might be related to the origins of pottery in the Central Sahara.
